insights.concise_text: Dedicated Question Answering (QA) systems address the health-information challenge by understanding natural language questions without relying on external information on the users.

triple.subject: Dedicated Question Answering (QA) systems
triple.object: the health-information challenge

insights.concise_text: Recognizing Question Entailment (RQE) supports Dedicated Question Answering (QA) systems by retrieving entailed questions with associated answers to answer premise questions.

triple.subject: Recognizing Question Entailment (RQE)
triple.object: Dedicated Question Answering (QA) systems

insights.concise_text: The paper evaluates the end-to-end RQE-based QA approach on TREC 2017 LiveQA medical questions by evaluating the relevance of the retrieved answers.

triple.subject: the end-to-end RQE-based QA approach
triple.object: TREC 2017 LiveQA medical questions

insights.concise_text: Because NLI definitions are not straightforwardly related to practical information retrieval or question answering systems, RQE has to be tailored to the question answering task.

triple.subject: NLI definitions
triple.object: RQE tailored to the question answering task

insights.concise_text: The inclusion of partial answers in question entailment implements the QA-specific requirement for relevant and meaningful relaxations of contextual and semantic constraints.

triple.subject: The inclusion of partial answers in question entailment
triple.object: relevant and meaningful relaxations of contextual and semantic constraints

insights.concise_text: The CMU-OAQA system used the Quora question-similarity dataset for training and achieved the best performance of 0.637 average score on the medical task.

triple.subject: The Quora question-similarity dataset
triple.object: the medical task with 0.637 average score

insights.concise_text: The performance gap between 1.139 on the LiveQA open-domain task and 0.637 average score on the medical task highlights the need for larger medical datasets.

triple.subject: The performance gap between 1.139 and 0.637 average score
triple.object: the need for larger medical datasets

insights.concise_text: Training attention-based decoder-encoder networks on the Quora dataset generalized better to the medical domain than training LSTMs on similar questions from Yahoo! and Answers.com.

triple.subject: Training attention-based decoder-encoder networks on the Quora dataset
triple.object: training LSTMs on similar questions from Yahoo! and Answers.com

insights.concise_text: The CMU-LiveMedQA system's average score of 0.353 was lower than systems relying on finding similar answered questions, supporting similar question matching for end-to-end QA.

triple.subject: The CMU-LiveMedQA system's average score of 0.353
triple.object: similar question matching for the end-to-end QA task

insights.concise_text: The empirical study's Logistic Regression choice is motivated by SemEval 2017 results where the best performing system achieved a MAP of 47.22% using supervised Logistic Regression.

triple.subject: a MAP of 47.22% using supervised Logistic Regression
triple.object: the empirical study's Logistic Regression choice

insights.concise_text: Because Logistic Regression trained on clinical-RQE data achieved 73.18% Accuracy on the 850 consumer health questions, the proposed QA system selected it to recognize and rank entailed questions.

triple.subject: 73.18% Accuracy on the 850 consumer health questions
triple.object: selection of Logistic Regression trained on the clinical-RQE dataset

insights.concise_text: The LR+IR method's best results on cQA-2016 and cQA-2017 led the proposed QA system to adopt a combination method merging search engine results and RQE scores.

triple.subject: best results on cQA-2016 and cQA-2017
triple.object: adoption of a combination method

insights.concise_text: Classifying the full QA collection for each test question is infeasible for real-time applications, so the proposed QA system first uses an IR method to retrieve candidate questions.

triple.subject: Classifying the full QA collection for each test question
triple.object: an IR method to retrieve candidate questions

insights.concise_text: The RQE-based QA system requires a collection of question-answer pairs, and the final collection contains 47,457 annotated question-answer pairs extracted from 12 trusted resources.

triple.subject: A RQE-based QA system
triple.object: 47,457 annotated question-answer pairs extracted from 12 trusted resources

insights.concise_text: The question types taxonomy derived from 1,721 consumer health questions supplied the manually defined triggers that were indexed with each question to improve retrieval.

triple.subject: the question types taxonomy
triple.object: indexing with manually defined question type triggers

insights.concise_text: Synonyms extracted during the crawl from National Institutes of Health web pages became the automatically extracted focus synonyms indexed with each question to avoid query expansion shortcomings.

triple.subject: synonyms of the main topic extracted during the crawl
triple.object: indexing with focus synonyms to avoid query expansion shortcomings

insights.concise_text: The hybrid IR+RQE QA system achieved 0.827 average score and 0.311 MAP@10 with 0.333 MRR@10, outperforming the IR-based QA system on first-answer and top-10 evaluations.

triple.subject: The hybrid IR+RQE QA system
triple.object: the IR-based QA system on first-answer and top-10 evaluations

insights.concise_text: The evaluation used TREC-2017 LiveQA medical test questions and LiveQA-Med reference answers, and the hybrid IR+RQE QA system achieved a higher score than the best LiveQA'17 medical challenge results.

triple.subject: The hybrid IR+RQE QA system
triple.object: TREC-2017 LiveQA medical test questions with LiveQA-Med reference answers

insights.concise_text: Because the average agreement on distinguishing Correct and Incorrect answers was 94.33% F1 score, the evaluations performed by assessor A were used for both methods.

triple.subject: 94.33% F1 score
triple.object: use of assessor A evaluations for both methods

insights.concise_text: The DL model with GloVe embeddings gave the best results on SNLI, MultiNLI and Quora, but SNLI and multi-NLI models did not perform well when tested on medical RQE data.

triple.subject: DL model with GloVe embeddings on SNLI, MultiNLI and Quora
triple.object: performance on medical RQE data

insights.concise_text: The RQE-based QA system outperformed the best TREC-2017 LiveQA medical results despite using only 47K medical question-answer pairs while LiveQA participating systems relied on much larger collections, including the World Wide Web.

triple.subject: RQE-based QA system
triple.object: best TREC-2017 LiveQA medical results with only 47K medical question-answer pairs

insights.concise_text: Because many LiveQA test questions had several subquestions while the system answered one subquestion at most, the hybrid IR+RQE approach has large potential for improvement of answer completeness.

triple.subject: one-subquestion-at-most limitation
triple.object: large potential for improvement of answer completeness in hybrid IR+RQE approach

insights.concise_text: The assessors' report that returned answers had correct question type but wrong focus supports future work on integrating a Question Focus Recognition module to enhance candidate question retrieval.

triple.subject: wrong-focus returned answers
triple.object: integration of a Question Focus Recognition module

insights.concise_text: The need to extend the medical QA collection with more information about drugs is supported by examples where ConsumerLab and eHealthMe answered drug questions when DailyMed lacked information.

triple.subject: ConsumerLab and eHealthMe drug-question examples
triple.object: extending the medical QA collection with more information about drugs

insights.concise_text: Private websites such as eHealthMe can answer drug questions when DailyMed lacks information, but patients' limited ability to validate such information motivates limitations on medical QA systems.

triple.subject: private websites answering drug questions
triple.object: limitations on medical QA systems in terms of the questions that can be answered

insights.concise_text: Strict guidelines based on information sources or HONcode are supported by experiments showing that limiting the number of answer sources with such guidelines could enhance QA performance from an information retrieval perspective.

triple.subject: experiments on limiting answer sources
triple.object: strict guidelines based on information sources or HONcode

insights.concise_text: The conclusion that the QA approach outperformed the best TREC-2017 LiveQA medical results is evidenced by RQE exceeding the best medical LiveQA'17 challenge results by a factor of 29.8%.

triple.subject: 29.8% improvement over best medical LiveQA'17 challenge results
triple.object: QA approach outperformed best TREC-2017 LiveQA medical results

insights.concise_text: For question number 36 in the TREC-2017 LiveQA medical test dataset, all submitted answers from 5 participating runs were wrong, while the IR-based QA system retrieved one excellent answer and hybrid IR+RQE provided 3 excellent answers.

triple.subject: question number 36
triple.object: IR-based QA system and hybrid IR+RQE outperforming 5 participating runs
